Penitent

PEN-ih-tent · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Penitent is feeling or showing sorrow and regret for having done wrong.

The penitent shoplifter returned to the store the next day to apologize and pay for everything he'd taken.

Worked Example

Standing penitent before the school board, the student admitted to copying his friend's homework and asked what he could do to make things right.

Penitent describes genuine remorse specifically tied to wrongdoing -- not just sadness, but sorrow over a mistake or a wrong committed.

How Penitent Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

remorseful

remorseful: feeling deep regret for a wrong committed

repentant

repentant: feeling or showing sincere regret about one's wrongdoing

Antonyms

unrepentant

unrepentant: not feeling shame or guilt about one's actions

defiant

defiant: boldly resistant or unwilling to comply, showing no regret

How Strong Is It? — apologetic → penitent → atone

apologetic vs. penitent

apologetic vs. penitent: A quick, apologetic 'sorry' can smooth over a minor bump with little real reflection.

atone vs. penitent

atone vs. penitent: This unit's own word atone goes further than penitent -- it describes taking real action to make up for a wrong, not just feeling sorry about it.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — poena

root — poena: punishment, penalty (Latin)

suffix — -ent

suffix — -ent: having the quality of (Latin -ens)

Put it together

Put it together: Penitent comes from Latin poenitere ("to make one regret"), rooted in poena ("punishment") -- someone penitent feels the weight of having earned a punishment for their wrong.

Word Choice
